mainTopic: Which ways of deriving law can pass a derived law on further: גזירה שוה, היקש, קל וחומר and בנין אב.
overview: This amud continues the sugya of 'למד מן הלמד': can a law that was itself derived go on to teach another law? It opens by finishing רמי בר חמא's proof that a law learned through a גזירה שוה can teach through another גזירה שוה. The burned bulls are cut up, not skinned. The גמרא then shows with a קל וחומר that a גזירה שוה-learned law can teach through a קל וחומר. It first builds that proof on רב פפא. Because not everyone accepts רב פפא, it rebuilds the proof on רמי בר חמא. Whether such a law can teach through a בנין אב stays unresolved, and the גמרא says תיקו. Next it turns to laws learned through a קל וחומר. Teaching through a היקש ends in תיקו, because that proof depends on רב פפא. Teaching through a גזירה שוה is proven. Teaching through another קל וחומר is proven only after a first proof is rejected as a 'grandson' of a קל וחומר. Finally, רבי ירמיה starts to show from רבי מאיר's argument about a bird given מליקה and found to be a טריפה that a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach through a בנין אב. That argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the proof: burned bulls are cut up, not skinned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes רמי בר חמא's proof. The same words 'skin, flesh, and dung' appear in two places, so the bulls here, like the bulls there, are burned after being cut into pieces without being skinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Torah says in the other place: 'skin, flesh, and dung.' Just as there, the animal is cut into pieces without being skinned, so too here, it is cut into pieces without being skinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof that started before this section. It shows that a law learned through a גזירה שוה can be passed on to another case through a second גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'skin, flesh, and dung' link two sets of burned bulls. The rule of the first set (cut up, not skinned) was itself learned through a גזירה שוה, yet it is passed on to the second set through another גזירה שוה. That shows a גזירה שוה-derived law can keep teaching through a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Below' or 'there': the other verse being compared.
Dung, the waste inside the animal's intestines.
Cutting the animal into its pieces or limbs.
Flaying, meaning removing the hide from the animal.

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof from רמי בר חמא becomes the backbone of the final answer in step 5.

phrases.english: And it is said there: skin, flesh, and dung;
just as there, it is by means of cutting into pieces
without flaying,
so too here, it is by means of cutting into pieces
without flaying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רמי בר חמא's proof, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: A law learned through a גזירה שוה can teach onward through another גזירה שוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared words 'skin, flesh, and dung' linking the two sets of burned bulls (ויקרא 4:11).

steps.title: Can a גזירה שוה-learned law teach through a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question: if a law was learned through a גזירה שוה, can it then teach another law through a קל וחומר?
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that was learned through a גזירה שוה: what is the law? Can it teach through a קל וחומר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question in the series about derived laws teaching onward. It sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא already showed that a גזירה שוה-derived law can teach through another גזירה שוה. Now it checks a different combination: גזירה שוה first, then קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that is learned, meaning a law that was itself derived from somewhere else.
Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both places.
A logical 'all the more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stricter one.
'What is it?', a standard way of asking what the law is.

phrases.english: A matter learned through a gezeira shava,
what is the law: may it teach through a kal vachomer?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from גזירה שוה to גזירה שוה (step 1) to a new pairing: גזירה שוה to קל וחומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law derived through a גזירה שוה can be the source for a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Answer through a קל וחומר based on רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. A היקש cannot teach through a היקש, yet it can teach through a קל וחומר. A גזירה שוה can even teach through a היקש (רב פפא), so surely it can teach through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can show it with a קל וחומר. A היקש cannot teach through another היקש (we know this from רבא or רבינא), yet it can teach through a קל וחומר (we know this from what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught). A גזירה שוה does teach through a היקש (we know this from רב פפא). Isn't it logical that it can teach through a קל וחומר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question using a קל וחומר. It compares the 'weaker' tool (היקש) with the 'stronger' tool (גזירה שוה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש is shown to be weak: a היקש-derived law cannot pass itself on through another היקש. Even so, it can pass itself on through a קל וחומר. A גזירה שוה is shown to be strong, since it can pass itself on even through a היקש, so it should certainly be able to pass itself on through a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the Torah places the two subjects side by side.
Teaches, meaning it passes its law on to another case.
Something taught in the study hall of רבי ישמעאל.
'Isn't it logical?', the closing line of a קל וחומר.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two levels. The question is about a law that was already learned through one method, and whether that law can then teach through a second method.

phrases.english: It can be shown by a kal vachomer:
And just as a hekesh, which does not teach through a hekesh,
as we know either from Rava or from Ravina,
phrases.notes: These are the proofs brought earlier on 49b.

phrases.english: still teaches through a kal vachomer,
as we know from what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught;
then a gezeira shava, which does teach through a hekesh,
as we know from Rav Pappa,
is it not logical that it should teach through a kal vachomer?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה הֶיקֵּשׁ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes: by a קל וחומר from היקש, which is weaker than גזירה שוה. The strength of גזירה שוה is proven from רב פפא.

steps.title: What about those who reject רב פפא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the answer depends on רב פפא. Someone who rejects רב פפא's view has no way to show that a גזירה שוה is stronger than a היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for someone who accepts רב פפא's teaching. But for someone who does not accept רב פפא's teaching, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 3. It says the proof only works if you accept רב פפא, and not everyone does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole קל וחומר rested on the claim that a גזירה שוה teaches through a היקש, and that claim came from רב פפא. If you reject רב פפא, that piece is missing, so the 'stronger' side of the argument is not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This works out well', said before raising a problem for another view.
For the one who holds of it, meaning accepts that teaching.
For the one who does not hold of it.
'What is there to say?', meaning how would that view answer.

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא;
phrases.english: This works well for the one who accepts the teaching of Rav Pappa;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: but for the one who does not accept the teaching of Rav Pappa,
phrases.notes: This is מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי, who argued with רב פפא earlier.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the foundation of the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of רב פפא in the קל וחומר of step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof depends on a disputed opinion, so it fails for anyone who rejects רב פפא.

steps.title: A new קל וחומר based on רמי בר חמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rebuilds the קל וחומר. It shows the strength of גזירה שוה from רמי בר חמא's proof that a גזירה שוה can teach through another גזירה שוה, and does not rely on רב פפא at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, use this קל וחומר. A היקש cannot teach through another היקש (from רבא or רבינא), yet it can teach through a קל וחומר (from the school of רבי ישמעאל). A גזירה שוה can teach through a second גזירה שוה (from רמי בר חמא). Isn't it logical that it can teach through a קל וחומר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by swapping out the disputed piece. Instead of רב פפא, it uses רמי בר חמא's proof, which was just finished in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'weak side' of the argument stays the same: a היקש cannot teach through a היקש, yet it still teaches through a קל וחומר. The 'strong side' is now proven differently: a גזירה שוה can teach through another גזירה שוה, while a היקש cannot do the same with another היקש. So גזירה שוה is still stronger, and it surely teaches through a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather', which signals a new, replacement answer.
Its fellow, meaning another גזירה שוה.

steps.whatToRemember: A law learned through a גזירה שוה CAN teach through a קל וחומר. The reasoning: even a היקש-derived law teaches through a קל וחומר, and a גזירה שוה is stronger than a היקש, as רמי בר חמא's proof shows.
steps.confusionAlert: Steps 3 and 5 look almost identical. Only the second half changed: 'teaches through a היקש (רב פפא)' became 'teaches through another גזירה שוה (רמי בר חמא)'.

phrases.english: Rather, use this kal vachomer:
And just as a hekesh, which does not teach through a hekesh,
as we know either from Rava or from Ravina,
still teaches through a kal vachomer,
as we know from what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught;

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, הַמְלַמֶּדֶת בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה חֲבֶירְתָּהּ –
phrases.english: then a gezeira shava, which teaches through another gezeira shava,
as we know from Rami bar Ḥama,
is it not logical that it should teach through a kal vachomer?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה הֶיקֵּשׁ, שֶׁאֵין מְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by replacing רב פפא with רמי בר חמא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the disputed source with an accepted one, keeping the same structure of argument.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without רב פפא, we might think there is no proof that a גזירה שוה is stronger than a היקש.
steps.terutzMaskana: רמי בר חמא shows a גזירה שוה teaches through another גזירה שוה, which a היקש cannot do, so the קל וחומר still holds.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A law learned through a גזירה שוה can teach through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Can a law learned by גזירה שוה teach through a בנין אב? Unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a law learned through a גזירה שוה can pass itself on through a בנין אב, and leaves the question open with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a law was learned through a גזירה שוה, can it teach another law through a בנין אב? Let the question stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question in the same series: can a גזירה שוה-learned law teach through a בנין אב? It finds no answer and says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3–5 showed that a גזירה שוה-learned law can teach through a קל וחומר. The proof that stands is the one in step 5, after step 4 challenged the proof in step 3. Now the גמרא swaps in a different method of teaching, the בנין אב. It has no proof either way, so the question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: A law that was itself learned from somewhere else (not written directly)
A 'paradigm': one case sets the pattern, and similar cases follow it
'Let it stand': the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: A matter that is learned through a verbal analogy,
what is the law: may it teach through a paradigm?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בְּבִנְיַן אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'learned-then-teaching' questions with a new pair of methods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law learned through a גזירה שוה can teach another law through a בנין אב.

steps.title: Can a law learned by קל וחומר teach through a היקש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can pass itself on through a היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a law was learned through a קל וחומר, can it teach another law through a היקש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, flipping the pair: now the law was learned by קל וחומר and wants to teach by היקש. The next step will try to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the 'learned' method was mostly גזירה שוה. Here the starting point is a law learned by קל וחומר, and the question is whether it may teach through a היקש, which is a strong, verse-based link.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one (a fortiori)
Two topics placed side by side in a פסוק, so they share laws
'What is it?': what is the law?

phrases.english: A matter that is learned through an a fortiori argument,
what is the law: may it teach through a juxtaposition?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After leaving step 6 unresolved, the גמרא moves to a new pair of methods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach another law through a היקש.

steps.title: A קל וחומר shows it can teach through a היקש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds a קל וחומר. A גזירה שוה cannot be learned from a היקש, yet it can teach through one (רב פפא). A קל וחומר can be learned from a היקש (תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל), so surely it can teach through a היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is a קל וחומר. A גזירה שוה cannot learn from a היקש (from רבי יוחנן), yet it can teach through a היקש (from רב פפא). A קל וחומר can learn from a היקש (from the school of רבי ישמעאל). Isn't it logical that it can also teach through a היקש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 7 with yes. It proves this with a קל וחומר that compares how strong a גזירה שוה is to how strong a קל וחומר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lighter' case is גזירה שוה: it is weaker, since it cannot be built on a היקש (רבי יוחנן), and still it can teach through a היקש (רב פפא). The 'stricter' case is קל וחומר: it is stronger here, since it can be built on a היקש (תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל). So if the weaker method can teach through a היקש, the stronger one surely can.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And just as...': the opening words of a קל וחומר
A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל: a קל וחומר can be built on a law from a היקש
'Is it not logical?': the closing words of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two directions apart: 'learned from' (where the law came from) and 'teaches through' (how it passes itself on). The proof compares the two methods on the 'learned from' side, then draws a result on the 'teaches through' side.

phrases.english: It is an a fortiori argument:
And just as a verbal analogy,
which cannot learn from a juxtaposition, as we see from רבי יוחנן,
still teaches through a juxtaposition, as we see from רב פפא;
then an a fortiori argument, which does learn from a juxtaposition
as we see from what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught,
is it not logical that it should teach through a juxtaposition?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, שֶׁאֵינָהּ לְמֵדָה בְּהֶיקֵּשָׁא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A law learned through a קל וחומר can teach through a היקש, proven by a קל וחומר built on רבי יוחנן, רב פפא, and תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: The proof depends on רב פפא, so the question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the proof only works for someone who accepts רב פפא. For someone who rejects him there is nothing to say, so the question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for someone who accepts רב פפא's view. But for someone who does not accept רב פפא, what can we say? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 8 because it rests on רב פפא. It finds no other support, so it ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 needed רב פפא to show that a גזירה שוה can teach through a היקש. Someone who rejects רב פפא loses that piece, and the קל וחומר falls apart. In step 5 a similar problem was fixed with רמי בר חמא's proof, but that proof only shows teaching through a גזירה שוה, not through a היקש, so here no fix is found.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This works well...': the start of 'fine for this view, but what about the other?'
'For one who holds' a certain view
'For one who does not hold' that view
'What is there to say?': no answer is available

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר is only as strong as the sources it stands on. If someone rejects one of those sources (here רב פפא), the proof no longer works for him, and the question stays תיקו.

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא – לְמַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא;
phrases.english: This works out well for one who accepts the view of רב פפא;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: but for one who does not accept the view of רב פפא,
what is there to say?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא – לְמַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 8 the same way step 4 challenged step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One of its building blocks, רב פפא's rule that a גזירה שוה teaches through a היקש, is not accepted by everyone. Without it the proof fails.
steps.terutzResolutionType: None. The question ends with תיקו.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach through a היקש stays unresolved for one who rejects רב פפא.

steps.title: Can a law learned by קל וחומר teach through a גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can pass itself on through a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a law was learned through a קל וחומר, can it teach another law through a גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens one more question in the series, this time about teaching through a גזירה שוה. The next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The starting point is the same as step 7 (a law learned by קל וחומר). The only change is the method of teaching, which is now a גזירה שוה instead of a היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two topics because the same word appears in both
'That it should teach': pass its law on to another case

phrases.english: A matter that is learned through an a fortiori argument,
what is the law: may it teach through a verbal analogy?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 ended in תיקו, the גמרא moves to a new pair of methods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach another law through a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: A קל וחומר built on רמי בר חמא shows it can teach through a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds a קל וחומר. A גזירה שוה cannot be learned from a היקש, yet it can teach through a גזירה שוה (רמי בר חמא). A קל וחומר can be learned from a היקש, so surely it can teach through a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is a קל וחומר. A גזירה שוה cannot learn from a היקש (from רבי יוחנן), yet it can teach through a גזירה שוה (from רמי בר חמא). A קל וחומר can learn from a היקש (from the school of רבי ישמעאל). Isn't it logical that it can also teach through a גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 10 with yes. It uses the same kind of קל וחומר as step 8, but swaps in רמי בר חמא in place of רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גזירה שוה is again the 'weaker' side: it cannot be built on a היקש, yet it can teach through a גזירה שוה, as רמי בר חמא proved. קל וחומר is 'stronger' because it can be built on a היקש, so it surely can teach through a גזירה שוה too. Since this proof uses רמי בר חמא and not רב פפא, the problem from step 9 does not come up here.

keyTerms.meaning: His proof ('skin, flesh, and dung') shows that a law from a גזירה שוה can teach through another גזירה שוה
'That it should teach': the same idea as שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד, in feminine form

steps.whatToRemember: The two קל וחומר proofs (steps 8 and 11) have the same shape. The only difference is the source that shows what a גזירה שוה can teach through: רב פפא (which not everyone accepts) for היקש, and רמי בר חמא for גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: It is an a fortiori argument:
And just as a verbal analogy,
which cannot learn from a juxtaposition, as we see from רבי יוחנן,

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה מִדְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא;
phrases.english: still teaches through a verbal analogy, as we see from רמי בר חמא;
then an a fortiori argument, which does learn from a juxtaposition
as we see from what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught,
is it not logical that it should teach through a verbal analogy?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, שֶׁאֵינָהּ לְמֵידָה בְּהֶיקֵּשָׁא מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with the same structure as step 8, built on רמי בר חמא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A law learned through a קל וחומר can teach through a גזירה שוה, proven by a קל וחומר built on רבי יוחנן, רמי בר חמא, and תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Can a law learned by a קל וחומר teach through another קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether something learned through a קל וחומר can then teach its law onward through a new קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a law was learned through a קל וחומר, can it then be used to teach another case through a קל וחומר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question in its series. Now it asks whether a law that came from a קל וחומר can pass itself on through another קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא asked whether a law learned by a קל וחומר can teach through a היקש or a גזירה שוה. Now both the source method and the teaching method are קל וחומר. The question is whether one קל וחומר can be built on top of another.

keyTerms.meaning: A law that was itself learned from somewhere else
What is the law? (opens a question)
That it should teach onward to another case

phrases.english: A matter that is learned through a kal vachomer,
what is the law: may it teach through a kal vachomer?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the series after Step 10–11 (קל וחומר teaching through גזירה שוה).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach onward through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: First proof from a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds a קל וחומר: a גזירה שוה, which is weaker, can teach through a קל וחומר, so a קל וחומר, which is stronger, surely can.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גזירה שוה cannot be learned from a היקש (רבי יוחנן), yet it can teach through a קל וחומר, as we said. A קל וחומר can be learned from a היקש (תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל). So it should surely be able to teach through a קל וחומר. This is a קל וחומר that comes from a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a קל וחומר. It compares the 'strength' of a גזירה שוה and a קל וחומר to show that a קל וחומר can teach through a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strength is measured by whether a method can be learned from a היקש. A גזירה שוה cannot, but a קל וחומר can, so the קל וחומר is stronger. If the weaker one can teach through a קל וחומר, the stronger one surely can. The גמרא adds that this proof is a קל וחומר built on a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one case from another through a shared word in the פסוקים
Comparing two things placed side by side in a פסוק
Isn't it logical? (the closing line of a קל וחומר)
A קל וחומר that is built on top of another קל וחומר

phrases.english: There is a kal vachomer:
Just as a gezeirah shavah,
which cannot be learned through a hekesh,
as we know from Rabbi Yochanan,
still teaches through a kal vachomer, as we said;
a kal vachomer, which can be learned from a hekesh
as we know from what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught,
isn't it logical that it can teach through a kal vachomer?!

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶהוּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר בֶּן קַל וָחוֹמֶר.
phrases.english: And this is a kal vachomer that is the son of a kal vachomer.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, שֶׁאֵינָהּ לְמֵידָה בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 using the same pattern of proof as Steps 8 and 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, by a קל וחומר from גזירה שוה, which is weaker than קל וחומר yet teaches through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: The proof is a grandson of a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: it is not a son but a grandson of a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. This is not a 'son' of a קל וחומר, it is a 'grandson' of a קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof it just gave. It says the proof stacks one קל וחומר too many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof relied on the fact that a גזירה שוה can teach through a קל וחומר ('as we said'). That fact was itself proven earlier with a קל וחומר. So the proof is a קל וחומר resting on a קל וחומר, and the law it teaches adds a third level. That is a grandson, and it goes too far.

keyTerms.meaning: Grandson; here, a third level of קל וחומר stacked on others
As we said; points back to something already proven earlier in the sugya
A קל וחומר two levels removed from the original

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the question being asked. The problem is the proof. Its starting point ('a גזירה שוה teaches through a קל וחומר') was itself learned through a קל וחומר, and that adds an extra level.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא!
phrases.english: It is the grandson of a kal vachomer!
phrases.notes: The 'as we said' in the proof points to something the גמרא already proved with a קל וחומר, so this stacks another layer on top.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the closing claim of Step 13 that this was only a קל וחומר בן קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from גזירה שוה in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Its starting point was itself learned through a קל וחומר, so the result is a third-generation קל וחומר.

steps.title: Second proof from a היקש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds a new קל וחומר from היקש, whose starting points come straight from sources, so it is only a קל וחומר בן קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is a קל וחומר. A היקש cannot be learned from a היקש (from רבא or from רבינא), yet it can teach through a קל וחומר (תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל). A קל וחומר can be learned from a היקש (תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל). So it should surely be able to teach through a קל וחומר. And this is only a קל וחומר בן קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected proof with a new one. This time it compares the קל וחומר to a היקש instead of a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש cannot be learned from a היקש, but a קל וחומר can, so here too the קל וחומר is stronger. Each starting point comes directly from a named source (רבא, רבינא, תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל), not from an earlier קל וחומר. So the proof is only one level deep, a קל וחומר בן קל וחומר, and it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; brings in a replacement after a rejection
Either ... or
A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר learned from a קל וחומר can teach through a קל וחומר. The proof must use starting points that come straight from sources, so it stays a 'son' and does not become a 'grandson.'

phrases.english: Rather, here is a kal vachomer:
Just as a hekesh, which cannot be learned through a hekesh,
as we know either from Rava or from Ravina,
still teaches through a kal vachomer
as we know from what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught;
a kal vachomer, which can be learned from a hekesh
as we know from what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught,
phrases.notes: The same teaching proves both points: the היקש taught a קל וחומר, which also means a קל וחומר was learned from a היקש.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that it can teach through a kal vachomer?!

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶהוּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר בֶּן קַל וָחוֹמֶר.
phrases.english: And this is a kal vachomer that is the son of a kal vachomer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה הֶיקֵּשׁ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ לָמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in Step 14 with one that is only one level deep.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, by a קל וחומר from היקש, whose starting points come directly from sources.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A law learned through a קל וחומר can teach through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Can a law learned by a קל וחומר teach through a בנין אב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach onward through a בנין אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a law was learned through a קל וחומר, can it then teach another case through a בנין אב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens the next question in the series. This time the teaching method is a בנין אב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source method stays the same (קל וחומר), and the teaching method changes to בנין אב. The question is whether a law that came from a קל וחומר can serve as the model case for a בנין אב.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'model case': building a general rule from one case and applying it to similar cases

phrases.english: A matter that is learned through a kal vachomer,
what is the law: may it teach through a binyan av?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בְּבִנְיַן אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New question in the series, after the קל וחומר question was settled in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach onward through a בנין אב.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה brings the משנה of a bird given מליקה and found to be a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה begins a proof from a משנה: a bird given מליקה and then found to be a טריפה. רבי מאיר says it does not make a person impure in the throat; רבי יהודה says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Come and hear. If the כהן did מליקה and the bird was found to be a טריפה, רבי מאיר says it does not make impure in the throat, and רבי יהודה says it does make impure in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה starts a proof for the question about בנין אב by quoting a משנה. This step sets up the case, and the proof itself will be explained next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה brings a dispute about a bird that had a valid מליקה but turned out to be a טריפה. Does it still make a person impure in the throat the way a dead bird does? רבי מאיר says no, and רבי יהודה says yes. Steps 18 and 19 show how this dispute connects to the question.

keyTerms.meaning: He pinched the bird's neck (מליקה), the way a bird offering is killed
An animal or bird with a fatal defect
The throat, where a person becomes impure when swallowing meat of a dead kosher bird
Makes a person impure

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Come and hear:
If he pinched the bird's neck and it was found to be a tereifah,
Rabbi Meir says:
It does not make impure in the throat.
phrases.notes: Meat of a dead kosher bird makes a person impure while he is swallowing it, as it passes through the throat.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
It does make impure in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 16 by quoting a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach through a בנין אב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a bird given מליקה and found to be a טריפה (dispute of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה).

steps.title: רבי מאיר's קל וחומר: slaughter purifies a bird that is a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר argues that since slaughter keeps an animal טריפה from carrying נבלה impurity, it surely does the same for a bird טריפה, whose נבלה impurity is weaker.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: This is a קל וחומר. An animal carcass makes a person impure by touching and by carrying, and still, slaughtering it keeps it from that impurity even when it is a טריפה. A bird carcass does not make a person impure by touching or carrying. Isn't it logical that slaughtering it also keeps a bird טריפה from its impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה from step 17. רבי מאיר explains his view with a קל וחומר from an animal to a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lenient' side is the bird, whose נבלה impurity is weaker (no impurity through touching or carrying). The 'strict' side is the animal, whose נבלה impurity is stronger, yet slaughter still removes it from a טריפה. So for the bird, slaughter should surely work too. For רבי ירמיה's proof, the key point is that this law about a bird is learned only through a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of an animal that died without proper slaughter
The carcass of a bird that died without proper slaughter
Touching and carrying, two ways impurity can pass to a person
Ritual slaughter with a knife
Makes pure, here meaning it keeps the animal from becoming impure

steps.confusionAlert: Slaughter does not make a טריפה kosher to eat. It only keeps the dead animal from carrying נבלה impurity.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said: it is a kal vachomer:
And just as the carcass of an animal,
which makes impure through touching and through carrying,
its slaughter purifies its tereifa from its impurity;
phrases.notes: He means that a טריפה animal that was slaughtered does not become an impure נבלה, even though you still may not eat it.

phrases.aramaic: נְבֵילַת עוֹף, שֶׁאֵין מְטַמֵּא בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא –
phrases.english: the carcass of a bird, which does not make impure through touching and carrying,
is it not logical that its slaughter
should purify its tereifa from its impurity?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה quoted in step 17, giving רבי מאיר's reasoning.
steps.raayaObject: Shows the first link: the law that slaughter purifies a bird טריפה is learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a bird given מליקה and found to be a טריפה (רבי מאיר's argument).

steps.title: רבי מאיר begins a comparison based on slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר begins a בנין אב: just as slaughter, which permits a bird to be eaten, also purifies its טריפה, the comparison will be applied to another case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as we found with slaughter, which makes the bird permitted for eating...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רבי מאיר starts a new comparison using slaughter as the model case, and the sentence finishes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law that slaughter purifies a bird טריפה was just learned by a קל וחומר in step 18. Now רבי מאיר uses that very law as the model for a בנין אב. If this works, it shows that a law learned through a קל וחומר can teach onward through a בנין אב, which answers the question from step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Just as we found', the opening words of a comparison to a model case
Learning a rule from a model case and applying it to a similar case
Makes it permitted to be eaten

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the step that ties רבי מאיר's argument to the question from step 16. The model for the בנין אב is a law that only came from a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Just as we found with slaughter,
phrases.notes: He means the slaughter of a bird, whose power to purify a טריפה we just learned in the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: that it makes it permitted for eating –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the result of the קל וחומר in step 18 by using it as the model case for a בנין אב.
steps.raayaObject: Shows the second link: a law learned by a קל וחומר is used as the model for a בנין אב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's argument in the משנה.
